title: Takeoff Runway: Velocity Slate
content:
Purpose:
A compact operational workbook for planning a staged launch that prioritizes velocity while keeping cost and quality guardrails intact. This is intentionally pragmatic—not a full checklist—designed for fast decision cycles and clear ownership across product, infra, and ops.

Scope:
- Feature surface: hosted API + Dedicated pool (initial), private deployments deferred to later waves.
- Traffic profile: conversational generation, short-to-medium average token lengths (~40 tokens/request).
- Risk appetite: moderate; prioritize availability and quality over aggressive cost-cutting for initial window.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- 2-week controlled ramp with 4 phased windows: alpha canary, expanded canary, controlled growth, scale release.
- Primary KPI focus: successful requests per second (sRPS), median request latency (ms), error rate 5xx (%), token-cost per 1k tokens (USD), quality drift score (prompt eval pass %).
- Circuit-breaker triggers defined for automated traffic rollback.

Key baseline KPIs (pre-launch snapshots):
- sRPS baseline (simulated): 45 rps stable
- Median latency target: < 220ms for p95=450ms
- Error rate target: < 0.8%
- Cost baseline: $1.80 per 1k tokens (hosted mix)
- Eval pass rate (smoke prompts): >= 92%

Launch windows and traffic plan (timeboxed):
- Window A (Alpha canary) — Day 0: 100 real users max, internal + beta customers. Duration: 24 hours. Purpose: smoke production plumbing, tracing, basic SLO validation.
- Window B (Expanded canary) — Day 1–2: 1–3 rps ramp for selected customer segments (10 customers). Duration: 48 hours. Purpose: load-profile validation, billing flow, quota enforcement.
- Window C (Controlled growth) — Day 3–7: Stepwise ramp to 40% projected capacity. Introduce synthetic burst tests outside business hours. Purpose: capacity tuning, autoscaler profile validation.
- Window D (Scale release) — Day 8–14: Move to open sign-up; monitor stability and cost metrics closely and keep autoscaler conservative for first 24h.

Canary mechanics and monitoring hooks:
- Canary tagging: route header X-Canary: true for 1% of traffic; controllers in infra to pick by hashed userId.
- Metrics to watch (real-time dashboard): total rps, sRPS by model variant, KV cache hit rate, queue length, GPU utilization, per-token cost estimate, quality drift (eval pass).
- Tracing: enable full sample traces for errors and 1 in 100 successful requests for latency profiles.

SLOs and circuit-breakers (auto actions):
- If 5xx rate > 1.5% for 10m -> automatic rollback to last stable model variant (automated route substitution) and page on-call.
- If p95 latency > 1s for 15m -> reduce concurrency limit and divert 30% of traffic to fallback (lower-capacity model variant).
- If cost per 1k tokens spikes > 40% vs baseline for 30m -> throttle non-critical batch jobs and notify finance/product for immediate triage.
- If quality eval pass drops > 6 percentage points -> pause new user onboarding and escalate to product + research.

Owner matrix (Who does what):
- Launch Lead: Priya Nair (product-ops) — overall go/no-go coordination, comms.
- Infra/Runtime: Elliot Chen (serving-runtime) — autoscaler tuning, routing rules, rollback wiring.
- Observability: Hannah Li (observability) — dashboards, alert thresholds, tracing.
- Customer Success: Marisol Vega — early customer comms, beta cohort management.
- Site Reliability: Tom O'Rourke (SRE) — runbooks, incident lead.

Acceptance criteria (per window):
- A: 0 critical errors, smoke eval pass >= 92%, no tracing anomalies.
- B: Queue lengths stable, p95 latency within 1.5x baseline, billing records verified for sample customers.
- C: Autoscaler behavior validated across cold-start patterns, KV cache hit rate stable +/-5%.
- D: Traffic stability for 48 hours, error rate < 1% and cost delta within expected envelope.

Tasks (short actionable items):
- Pre-flight (owners):
  - Create canary routing rule + test harness (Elliot) — verify header propagation and hash consistency.
  - Lock model version and record hash in release artifact (product) — tie to rollback mapping.
  - Setup smoke eval suite and schedule (Hannah/Product) — add 50 prompts with edge-cases.
  - Communicate beta list + SLAs to CS (Marisol) — ensure support channels staffed.
- During launch:
  - 15-minute cadence ops check-ins for first 12h (Priya)
  - Monitor canary telemetry; if any SLO triggers, execute remediation runbook (Tom)
  - Record every anomaly in the runbook spreadsheet with timestamp, owner, action taken (Hannah)

Risk register (top items + mitigations):
- Risk: Model quality regression discovered only under production traffic. Mitigation: staggered rollout + prepopulated evals + immediate rollback.
- Risk: Autoscaler thrashes at burst extremes. Mitigation: conservative initial concurrency + synthetic burst testing off-peak.
- Risk: Billing spikes from token-heavy adversarial prompts. Mitigation: token quota enforcement + rate-limiting by client tier.

Contingency play snippets (quick references):
- Immediate rollback: set routing to stable-model-v1 -> notify product+infra -> run postmortem after containment.
- Soft-throttle: apply per-route QPS cap to non-critical routes and degrade to truncated responses for heavy callers.
- Customer-facing incident: CS to send initial templated note within 30 minutes, then follow-up with root-cause estimate within 6 hours. Template link: (see linked artifacts).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we allow preflight traffic shaping by geography or only by customer ID hashing? (Product / Infra decision)
- What is the escalation SLA for quality regressions (90m vs 4h)?
- Confirm the exact token-cost threshold that triggers finance paging.

Communication plan:
- Internal: #launch-control Slack channel; 15-minute huddles first 12h, then 30-minute for next 48h.
- External: Beta customers notified 24h before window A; broad announcement scheduled only after Window C success.

Post-launch evaluation (week 1 and week 4 checkpoints):
- Week 1: Stability review, cost reconciliation, quick wins list, outstanding risks.
- Week 4: Adoption metrics vs forecast, model quality regression analysis, decision on Dedicated pool sizing adjustments.

Appendix: quick checks (to run before each window):
- [ ] Release artifact exists with immutable model hash.
- [ ] Canary routing implemented and smoke header verified.
- [ ] Smoke eval suite passes locally and in staging.
- [ ] Rollback playbook rehearsed in staging.
- [ ] CS has customer list and incident templates.
- [ ] Finance alerted and watching cost dashboards.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: Drafted by Priya Nair
- 2025-11-20: Added canary mechanics and SLOs (Elliot)
- 2026-02-28: Incorporated autoscaler tuning notes after staging wargame (Hannah)

Notes to self: keep this doc lean. If a section grows beyond ~300 words, move to a dedicated playbook and link it.

Related tickets: PROJ-3185 (canary routing), PROJ-3190 (autoscaler tuning), PROJ-3221 (smoke evals).

End of workbook.
